title: Charlie Wagner stories and losing old friends
summary: Wagner's Jean Lafitte Rose publicity stunt, his Lafitte job with no union, and Hirsch's sadness at losing Ray Bonitas and other friends.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I still got the picture of it. So we go up to somewhere, by the school, by the library up there. And we get a little girl and dress her up in like a little pirate's costume with a bandana around her head like this. And we're both standing there. And I got a shovel, and Charlie's there pointing at it. And we're planting that Jean Lafitte rose in the ground. And that's what got in the newspaper. We got it in the newspaper and we had it all over town. The Jean Lafitte Rose. When the British are coming, it turns red. He could think of the craziest things. He, he, this is another thing about Charlie. He was in Lafitte, Louisiana, and had a band over there, and didn't have a job, and he needed a trombone player. And he called a fella by the name of Mexic, who was still alive and in our union. Joe Mexic. He's playing a job over in Birmingham. He wasn't satisfied. He wanted to be closer to home. And Charlie rings him up and says, I got a good job over here. Why don't you come over here? So he puts his job over there. And he comes along, he comes to Lafitte, and he meets Charlie at the, at the, at the railroad station. And it's a hot day, and he says, let's take a cab. It's too hot to walk. He says, no, there's no walk. It's good walking. It's good for you. You didn't have the money to get a cab. So when he finally got over to where they were, staying, what time is the job time? Charlie says, there ain't no job. He says, we got fired. He says, what do you mean? He says, I quit a job to come over here. He says, when I go back, go back to New Orleans, I'm going to put you up before the union. Charlie says, you can't do that. He says, why? He says, because we don't belong to the union.

Would you believe that? We don't belong to the union. But this is something that little Ray Vanitas. He could, he could remind you of things like that. This is one thing we used to talk about. Ray was a very dear friend of mine. And I sure hated to lose him. I hated to lose my other old boy. I think I have a bad luck with baseball is. Really? I lost three. Three. Yeah, that's right. Yeah. Pat Easterling, Ray and Frank. I didn't expect to lose Frank so soon. Ray rang up my wife, she used to talk to my wife and said, tell Godfrey to throw his heart medicine away. To take garlic. That's the latest thing. She says, that's what Kerry Graham died from. He said, no. He says, that's good for you. He died in two weeks.
